abstract: This essay examines what the Great Reset means from a cognitive security perspective, analyzing how global socioeconomic narratives shape public belief and behavior. Through the lens of Active Inference, narrative ecosystems, and information theory, the paper explores how large-scale narrative shifts can either empower or disempower individuals and communities in their sensemaking processes.

methods.name: Edited volume compiling COGSEC's 2020 work in six chapters
methods.description: Friedman and Cordes edit six chronologically ordered chapters by COGSEC and collaborators on remote teams, operations orders, and maps.
methods.evidence: This edited volume is a compilation of the traces that COGSEC and collaborators left during 2020.

methods.name: Complexity Science analysis of counterinsurgency team assembly (Ch. 1)
methods.description: Cordes and Friedman use a Complexity Science framework, starting from a 2008 Mumbai attack vignette, to study rapid team assembly in counterinsurgency.
methods.evidence: This paper uses a Complexity Science framework to investigate the relationship between the rapid assembly of teams and the success of counterinsurgency and related efforts.

methods.name: Systems Engineering ONFT assessment with Active Inference (Ch. 3)
methods.description: Vyatkin et al. use Systems Engineering to define Ontologies, Narratives, Formal documents, and Tools (ONFT) for remote teams, explored via Active Inference.
methods.evidence: We suggest that Systems Engineering provides guidelines to define the functions of Ontologies, Narratives, Formal documents, and Tools (ONFT) within the context of the life cycle of any System of Interest.

methods.name: Historical review of Operations Orders (Chs. 4 and 6)
methods.description: Chapters trace military and business Operations Orders from antiquity to the present to inform new catechism-style formats.
methods.evidence: This paper discusses the origins and evolution of Operations Orders from antiquity to modern times and the impact of Operations Orders on organizational sensemaking.

methods.name: Responses to DARPA Polyplexus incubator prompts (Chs. 2 and 5)
methods.description: Chapters 2 and 5 were written in response to Polyplexus incubators on remote culture for pandemics and on reimagining maps.
methods.evidence: Infinite Games for Infinite Teams was written in response to and published through DARPA Polyplexus Citizen Science Incubator: Inventing a Remote Culture to Deal with Pandemics (Incubator-ID 399).

key_findings: The editors report that Chapter 1 found rapid reorganization, resilience, and integration of new information channels to be instrumental for both terrorist and counterterrorist activity.

Chapter 4 (Cordes and Friedman) found that changes in technological and organizational complexity historically required new OPORD formats, and proposes a Facilitator's Catechism building on the Heilmeier Catechism.
Chapter 6 (Cordes, Friedman, Phelan) presents an Innovator's Catechism, a catechism-styled operations order for early-stage innovation teams derived from the Facilitator's Catechism.
Chapter 2 contributes role-based improvisational and cultural dynamics for rapidly assembled online teams and initial "Infinite Game" structures for research and citizen science.
The editors note COGSEC came to see knowledge management as fundamentally social and collaborative, beyond computational tools and data standards.
key_findings_evidence: We found that the capacity to reorganize rapidly, maintain resilience, and integrate new information channels are instrumental for both successful terrorist and counterterrorist activity.
We found that historically, changes in technological and organizational complexity necessitated novel formats and applications of OPORDs.
presents the “The Innovator’s Catechism”, a catechism-styled operations order for use by early-stage innovation teams.
the provision of several initial “Infinite Game” structures with application in research, development, and citizen science domains.
we came to understand that knowledge management is a fundamentally social and collaborative process.

summary_provenance.method: Evidence-grounded extraction from full_text.md: every method and finding carries a verbatim quote from the paper text, mechanically verified to occur in full_text.md (whitespace/ligature-normalized) before merge.
summary_provenance.notes: Multi-author edited book (COGSEC, ISBN 978-1-7364269-0-6); bibliography lists no authors, but the volume is edited by Daniel A. Friedman & Richard J. Cordes. Findings are largely the editors' foreword summaries of each chapter's contribution and are attributed to chapters; no empirical studies.
